status_summary: Two parts are operative or advancing and one is largely blocked in court. DHS published a final rule on 2025-12-29, effective 2026-02-27, replacing the random H-1B cap lottery with a selection weighted toward higher-skilled and higher-paid beneficiaries, starting with the FY2027 registration season. The Labor Department proposed on 2026-03-27 to raise all four prevailing-wage levels (Level I from about the 17th to the 34th percentile, Level IV from the 67th to the 88th); the text keeps four levels, so it does not eliminate the two lowest as the Mandate asks, and the rule is not final. Proclamation 10973 (signed 2025-09-19) required a 100,000 dollar payment for H-1B workers abroad, and Proclamation 11069 (signed 2026-09-18) extended it to 2027-09-21 with the payment unchanged. Courts have split on the payment: a D.D.C. court upheld it on 2025-12-23 (appeal filed 2025-12-31); a D. Mass. court (State of California v. Mullin, No. 25-13829, Judge Sorokin) vacated the implementing policy on 2026-06-08, holding the payment an unauthorized tax and the policy issued without notice and comment and beyond statutory authority, then temporarily stayed its own order on condition that the government seek a stay from the First Circuit, which denied a stay on 2026-07-24; and an N.D. Cal. court (Global Nurse Force v. Trump) barred enforcement of implementing policies for both proclamations on 2026-09-30 until the agencies comply with notice-and-comment rulemaking. DHS also proposed on 2026-08-25 a 103,265 dollar fee on cap-subject petitions (comments closed 2026-09-24), and Executive Order 14431 (2026-09-18) directs agencies to coordinate on H-1B integrity and layoff-related review without changing wage levels.

timeline.event: Proclamation 10973 restricts entry of H-1B workers unless the employer pays 100,000 dollars, effective 2025-09-21 for 12 months unless extended, with DHS waiver authority.

Judge Beryl Howell (D.D.C.) upholds the proclamation on summary judgment in Chamber of Commerce v. DHS (No. 1:25-cv-03675), dated 2025-12-23; the Chamber files an appeal to the D.C. Circuit on 2025-12-31.
DHS publishes the final rule on weighted selection for cap-subject H-1B registrations, favoring higher-skilled and higher-paid beneficiaries, effective 2026-02-27 for the FY2027 registration season.

Labor Department proposes to raise the four prevailing-wage levels for H-1B, PERM and related programs to the 34th, 52nd, 70th and 88th percentiles (from about the 17th, 34th, 50th and 67th); comments closed 2026-05-26.

Judge Leo Sorokin (D. Mass.), in State of California v. Mullin (No. 25-13829-LTS), grants summary judgment to twenty states and vacates in its entirety the agency policy implementing Proclamation 10973's 100,000 dollar payment. The court holds that the payment is a tax that the proclamation's statutory authorities (INA 212(f) and 215(a)) do not delegate, and that the policy is a legislative rule issued without notice and comment, exceeds statutory authority and is arbitrary and capricious; it grants no separate injunction. The government appeals to the First Circuit on 2026-06-11 (per Ogletree and Barnes & Thornburg), the district court temporarily stays its own order on condition that the government seek a stay from the First Circuit by 2026-06-18 (per National Law Review), and the First Circuit denies a stay on 2026-07-24 (per Fredrikson & Byron and National Law Review), so the vacatur is in effect.

timeline.event: DHS proposes a 103,265 dollar filing fee for all cap-subject H-1B petitions, in addition to other fees; comments closed 2026-09-24.

Proclamation 11069 extends the entry restriction to 2027-09-21 with the 100,000 dollar payment unchanged and DHS waiver authority; Executive Order 14431, signed the same day, directs State, Labor and DHS to coordinate on H-1B integrity and consider employer layoffs.

In Global Nurse Force v. Trump (N.D. Cal., No. 4:25-cv-08454, Judge Gilliam), the court bars USCIS, CBP and the State Department from enforcing policies implementing the 100,000 dollar payment under Proclamations 10973 and 11069 unless and until they comply with Administrative Procedure Act rulemaking requirements; the Civil Rights Litigation Clearinghouse document list describes the order (ECF 130) as granting in part a motion for a preliminary injunction. The government filed a notice of appeal to the Ninth Circuit on 2026-10-09 (per Bloomberg Law).
